questions.question: Explain the difference between fair trade and unfair trade.
questions.expected_answer: Trade is fair when everyone involved is treated fairly and receives a fair share: producers get prices that cover their costs and let them live decently, workers earn fair wages in safe conditions, and nobody is forced to work. Trade is unfair when some people, such as farmers or workers, receive far less than a fair share or are treated badly, while others make large profits.

questions.question: Describe two examples of the human cost of unfair trade.
questions.expected_answer: Exploitation, where workers are paid too little and made to work very long hours. Unsafe working conditions, such as the Rana Plaza factory building in Bangladesh that collapsed in 2013, killing more than one thousand one hundred people. Child labour, where more than one hundred million children work in ways that harm them or keep them out of school, for example on some cocoa or cotton farms.

questions.question: Describe three ways in which trade can be made fairer.
questions.expected_answer: Governments can make and enforce laws on minimum wages, working hours, safety and child labour. Trade unions let workers join together to ask for fair pay and safe conditions. Fair trade organisations make sure producers get fair prices and label products that meet their standards. Consumers can ask how products were made and choose fair trade goods.
